parts.label: (b)(i)
hints: Hint 1: Calculate the incident photon energy using $E = \frac{hc}{\lambda}$ with $h = 6.63 \times 10^{-34}\text{ J s}$, $c = 3.00 \times 10^8\text{ m s}^{-1}$, and $\lambda = 280\text{ nm}$.
Hint 2: Convert the work function energy $\Phi = 3.4\text{ eV}$ to joules using $1\text{ eV} = 1.60 \times 10^{-19}\text{ J}$.
Hint 3: Use Einstein's photoelectric equation $E_{k,\text{max}} = hf - \Phi$ to determine the maximum kinetic energy of the emitted electrons.
Hint 4: Relate maximum kinetic energy to maximum speed using $E_{k,\text{max}} = \frac{1}{2}m_e v_{\text{max}}^2$ with electron mass $m_e = 9.11 \times 10^{-31}\text{ kg}$.
Hint 5: Solve for $v_{\text{max}}$ and express your answer to 2 significant figures with correct SI units ($\text{m s}^{-1}$).
